issues.description: The datasheet says the data were processed in Excel and describes code for converting raw data, but the delivered syntax begins with in-memory DataSet1/DataSet2 names and contains no GET/import or raw-response producer. The two observation-level datasets, exact schemas, Condition crosswalk, final-sample/exclusion rules, and Excel processing steps are not supplied. Request author-prepared analysis inputs and their codebook, or the actual raw-to-analysis producer specification; do not infer new participant recruitment from the historical experiments.

The six table blocks are substantive code embedded in a PDF, not a standalone .sps driver. The 18 *Table N, Panel X headings have no period and are followed immediately by commands; under interactive SPSS syntax, an asterisk heading is a comment and needs a terminator or separating blank line, so it can consume the following command. The printed page breaks also split the Table 3 final T-TEST and Table 6 first T-TEST across page footers/blank lines. Extract only the syntax, remove page artifacts, rejoin those continuations, and add periods to the heading comments in a working copy. The Table 4 final T-TEST has blank lines after its unperioded CI line, which SPSS 26 documents as an interactive terminator; no defect is asserted there.

The datasheet names SPSS version 26, but both Table 6 T-TEST blocks use /ES DISPLAY(TRUE), and IBM's T-TEST release history says the ES subcommand was introduced in release 27. IBM distinguishes DISPLAY, which controls effect-size output/estimation, from STANDARDIZER, whose paired-sample restriction does not make DISPLAY irrelevant to independent-samples tests. Keep the authored ES DISPLAY lines and resolve whether the documented runtime version or the supplied effect-size syntax is authoritative; do not silently remove the effect-size output.

evidence.quote:
Data Analyses
Table 1, Experiment 1
We used a 2 × 2 analysis of variance (ANOVA) to test the effect of our independent variables, repetit and
interact, on our dependent variable, Occ_exp_abs_percent. The following SPSS syntax generated results
reported in Table 1.

*Table 1, Panel A
DATASET ACTIVATE DataSet1.
MEANS TABLES=Occ_exp_abs_percent BY Condition
 /CELLS=MEAN STDDEV COUNT.

*Table 1, Panel B
UNIANOVA Occ_exp_abs_percent BY Repetit Interact
 /METHOD=SSTYPE(3)
 /INTERCEPT=INCLUDE
 /CRITERIA=ALPHA(0.05)
 /DESIGN=Repetit Interact Repetit*Interact.
evidence.description: Embedded SPSS syntax activates DataSet1 and supplies Table 1 MEANS, UNIANOVA, and design terms.

evidence.quote: An optional keyword that determines whether the effect size table is printed. TRUE is the default setting, which invokes the estimation of effect size.
